searchText: Yep this makes sense, seems inverse is still comparatively slow, so benefits start at 2 I’m on mobile, so I can’t parse this at the moment 😅 There is ns/op and ns/value , is the latter something you added? Trying to figure out the performance gain when you use batch trick with 2 No worries, we are nocturnal 😬 yes, the `ns/value` is a custom metric I added. It's basically `ns/op` divided by the sub-test case N batched values So for example, when batching for 64 points, it takes 35094 ns, which "per value" is ~548.4ns (35094/64) So I compare 1506 ns/op to the ns/value for the multiple benchmarks? Yes, that's the idea Okay makes sense 🙏 So for 2 it’s 1125 ns per value versus 1506 ns per value without the batch trick — about 23% diff Eager to see the overall diff from this 😬 PR looks good to me, changing the api to receive the slice instead of allocating in the function seems like a minor stylistic change, unless the common code path already has a slice allocated. Thank you for pointing that out in the PR though 🙏 Haven't tried MultiMapToField yet, I am finishing a big refactor before I can roll it in sounds too good to be true, I'm going to run it on the block replay a bit later today It makes no sense to apply it now, as I have this big refactor in the pipe. I'll ping you when it's ready. A couple days at most. My refactor includes using `MultiMapToField` in one location, but I'm sure that you will be able to squeeze even more. You go to bed late and I rise up early... the sun never sets on the verkle empire 🤣 This is consistent with what Gotti announced, and that's great because there are quite a few use cases in which two `toFr` are called in a row. <@427491045308235776> `MultiMapoToBaseFieldBytes` isn't quite what is needed, I think, because it returns a slice of byte arrays, when, to be useful when computing a node's commitment, it needs to calculate the base field proper, not get its bytes. So what I'd like to have is something along the lines of`MultiMapToBaseField(elements []*Element) []*Fr`, which shouldn't be too hard to write looking at the code. Incidentally, there's a ~10% speedup using the new inverse method and my refactor I want to try a couple more things (including `MultiMapToBaseField`) before I merge it to master. Oh, why do you need the Field and not the bytes? I didn’t expose it because its seemed not necessary and having the base field (Fp) alongside the scalar field (Fr) is sometimes confusing 😅 Will check again to see the code path! If you had it on hand, how much did the inverse method save? Would be good to see the relationship between a x% increase in inverse leading to a y% increase in the overall code for example. (If you had it beforehand, no worries if not)
